study_identification.title: Closing the life-cycle of normative modeling using federated hierarchical Bayesian regression

study_characteristics.study_objective: Proposes a federated hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) framework to complete the life-cycle of normative modeling on decentralized multi-site neuroimaging data, handling site effects, enabling parameter updating/extension, and model adaptation for local clinical deployment.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Permutation tests (1000 repetitions) with FDR correction across 148 regions; significant and stable regions reported if significant in ≥9/10 runs.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: HBR provides accurate normative ranges and mitigates site-effects relative to naive pooling and ComBat-based pooling; supports federated estimation, sequential extension, and parameter transfer for local adaptation; deviations quantified via z-scores/Pabn show disease-related abnormalities across regions.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Across multi-site ROI-wise cortical thickness, HBR and fixed-effect pooling achieve superior regression fit (RHO↑, SMSE↓, MSLL↓) versus naive pooling, harmonized pooling, and no-pooling. HBR uniquely supports site random effects with partial pooling, enabling centralized and decentralized training and adaptation to new centers (few-shot). In anomaly detection, deviation-based indices (z, Pabn) yield significant and stable region-wise AUCs for multiple diagnoses after permutation and FDR correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: (1) Gaussian residual assumption may miscalibrate centiles/z-scores for non-Gaussian phenotypes; authors note non-Gaussian extensions in follow-up work. (2) ROI-wise (univariate) modeling does not capture inter-regional covariance, leaving residual multivariate site-effects exploitable by classifiers. (3) While HBR removes site-effects from z-statistics, site-related variance remains in predictions (fμ); HBR is not a general-purpose harmonization replacement.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Quality control using FreeSurfer Euler number is critical at scale. Parameter transfer (informative hyperpriors) enables adapting reference models to small local datasets without sharing raw data, supporting privacy-preserving clinical deployment.

general_notes.general_notes: Datasets used (16): ABCD; CAMCAN; CMI; CNP; FCON; HCP; HCPAG; HCPDV; HCPEP; IXI; NKI; OASIS3; OPN; PNC; TOP; UKBB. Implementation uses PyMC3 and PCNToolkit v0.18; ComBat comparator implemented via neurocombat_sklearn.
